chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I never entered [the state of Ihram for Hajj] except as a Mutamatti', except in this year. For by Allah, I do not finish the Sa'i until my molars are chattering [from hunger/exertion], and the 'Adh' you performed is superior. If it is said: 'How do they say that the obligatory act is Tamattu', while they have divided Hajj into three types: Tamattu', Ifrad, and Qiran?' Then, if the matter were as you claim, this division would have no benefit.'

key_terms.أَضْرَاسِي: Adraasi (my molars/tears, indicating shivering from hunger or cold)
key_terms.الإِفْرَاد: Ifrad (a type of Hajj where one performs only Hajj)
key_terms.التَّمَطُّع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj separately)
key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'i (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.الْقِرَان: Qiran (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and Hajj together)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the three types of Hajj (Tamattu', Ifrad, Qiran) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the juristic debate regarding the obligatory nature of Hajj al-Tamattu' by highlighting the physical intensity of the ritual, noting that the interval between Umrah and Hajj is so brief that his teeth chatter from exertion. He employs a logical argument (*burhan*) against those who claim Tamattu' is the only valid form, asserting that the existence of distinct categories (Ifraad and Qiran) in scholarly discourse would be redundant if Tamattu' were exclusively obligatory, thereby validating the plurality of Hajj types.
